section_1.title: The Hook: The Chaos of Individuality
section_1.content: Introduce the idea that individual data points can be chaotic and follow any distribution (uniform, skewed, etc.). Establish prerequisite: Define 'Sample Mean' as the average of a small group of observations.
section_1.example: Imagine 1,000 squirrels collecting acorns. Some find 0, some find 50. The individual distribution is wild and messy.

section_2.title: The Experiment: From Chaos to Order
section_2.content: Visualize the process of taking multiple random samples from the population and calculating the mean for each. Show how the distribution of these 'means' starts to stabilize as the sample size increases.
section_2.example: An animation showing 100 groups of 30 squirrels each. Each group's average acorn count is plotted as a single dot on a new graph.

section_3.title: The Big Reveal: The Normal Distribution
section_3.content: Formally state the CLT: No matter the shape of the original population, the distribution of sample means will converge to a Normal Distribution (Bell Curve) as sample size increases. Emphasize that the center of this curve is the population mean.
section_3.example: The chaotic 'squirrel histogram' morphing smoothly into a perfect, symmetrical Bell Curve as the sample size grows.

section_4.title: Key Conditions for Validity
section_4.content: Highlight the two critical requirements: 1. Samples must be independent and random. 2. Sample size (n) should be sufficiently large (typically n ≥ 30). Explain that this is why '30' is the magic number in statistics.
section_4.example: A 'Checklist' graphic: Random? Yes. Independent? Yes. n ≥ 30? Yes. Result: Bell Curve unlocked!

section_5.title: The 'Why It Matters' Application
section_5.content: Explain that CLT allows us to make predictions about populations using only a sample, which is the foundation of inferential statistics and confidence intervals.
section_5.example: A factory manager using the CLT to predict the average battery life of 10,000 robots by testing only 30, saving time and resources.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)
